source.title: Stationary Points of Shallow Neural Networks with Quadratic Activation Function
source.authors: D. Gamarnik; Eren C. Kızıldağ; Ilias Zadik

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves generalization results for interpolating quadratic networks using a different architecture and a geometric sample condition, bearing conceptually on width and generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, ReLU width sweeps, or the optimizer, batch size, regularization, or measured-property versions. Its results are theoretical claims, not experimental measurements.
record.test_reason: The study proves generalization and optimization guarantees for realizable quadratic networks. It does not establish whether increasing width beyond interpolation lowers test error, as V2 claims. Its width-independent zero-risk guarantee under a sample-span condition concerns a related but different proposition. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarizes the sample-complexity conclusions: sufficient training-data span guarantees zero population risk for every interpolator, including wider ones; without that span, positive-risk interpolators exist for full-rank teachers. This is an existence statement below the threshold, not a claim that every interpolator generalizes poorly. The paper also proves conditional gradient-descent recovery guarantees and initialization guarantees for sufficiently wide randomly generated teachers.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical results for realizable shallow networks with quadratic activation; no experimental width sweep or ReLU training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The result depends on whether the training outer products span the full space of symmetric matrices; the paper identifies N* = d(d + 1)/2 as the almost-sure threshold for jointly continuous data.

fits_no_version.finding: Every exact quadratic-network interpolator has zero population risk if the training-input outer products span the symmetric matrices, regardless of interpolator width. For i.i.d. jointly continuous inputs, this condition holds almost surely when N ≥ d(d+1)/2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In realizable quadratic networks, sufficient training-data span guarantees perfect generalization for every interpolator independently of width.

fits_no_version.finding: If the span condition fails, a full-rank teacher admits positive-population-risk interpolators of any width at least d. Below N = d(d+1)/2, additional distributional assumptions yield an explicit lower bound for an existing bad interpolator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact interpolation alone does not guarantee generalization in realizable quadratic networks below the sample-span threshold.

record.problems: The evidence is a theoretical result in a stylized realizable quadratic-network model, not an empirical width sweep; generalization depends on the stated span condition.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results for the listed versions were found in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization, including chance performance on held-out random labels.
Whether widening a trained network beyond the width needed for zero training error continues to lower test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes to training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Correlation and ranking performance of magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The central mismatch is the tested proposition, not the use of theoretical evidence. Width-independent perfect generalization does not establish that further widening keeps lowering test error. The paper's discussion connecting its theorems to empirical overparameterization does not supply the missing width comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance are not studied.
No width sweep or test-error curve is reported; the result concerns quadratic activation and exact interpolation under a training-data span condition.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers are not compared.
Adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers are not compared.
Batch sizes and training budgets are not compared.
Sharpness or other trained-network measures are not related to the generalization gap.
Training examples are not removed or compared by memorization.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with quadratic activation; interpolating weight matrix W
rows.size_stated: arbitrary width m̄ ∈ N; m̄ may be larger than the teacher width m
rows.operation_detail: Proves that every interpolator has zero generalization error when the training inputs' outer products span all symmetric matrices.

conditions.value: span{Xi Xiᵀ : 1 ≤ i ≤ N} is the space of all d × d symmetric real-valued matrices

rows.uncertainty: Theorem states the result deterministically under its conditions; randomized-data result is with probability one when N ≥ N* = d(d + 1)/2 and the distribution is jointly continuous.
rows.note: The theorem allows interpolator width to exceed the teacher width; it does not report a width sweep or test-error curve.
rows.check: The zero-population-risk theorem is accurately summarized, but it does not compare test error across widths or show continued improvement after interpolation. Arbitrary interpolator width is not evidence for V2's decreasing-error claim. The operation is a theoretical proof, not a measurement.

rows.subject: shallow neural network with quadratic activation; interpolating weight matrix W
rows.operation_detail: Proves existence of an interpolator with positive generalization error when the training inputs' outer products do not span all symmetric matrices.

conditions.value: span{Xi Xiᵀ : 1 ≤ i ≤ N} is a strict subset of the symmetric matrices
any jointly continuous distribution on Rᵈ for the positive-error conclusion

rows.uncertainty: Existence result under stated conditions; no numerical estimate in Theorem 2.10(b).
rows.note: The text gives a quantitative lower bound under Theorem 2.13(b)'s additional i.i.d. centered-coordinate and N < N* conditions.
rows.check: Existence of a positive-risk interpolator when the span condition fails does not measure V2's width effect. It neither identifies the solution selected by gradient training nor compares widths. The result is an existence theorem, not a partially observed width trend. The quantitative bound in Theorem 2.13(b) is min{µ4−µ2², 2µ2²}σmin(W*)⁴; '1/1' is not a reported result.
